texte.Sous le classement, chaque pays a sa fic: Below the ranking, each country has its expandable record: ADVANTAGES and DISADVANTAGES in two columns, an arbitration COMMENT, then the outlook to # — dated and sourced investment announcements (InvestAI, Paris Summit, AWS Aragon, Stargate Norway…) distinguished from observed CONSTRAINTS: Dublin’s grid connection moratorium, Dutch restrictions on hyperscale, the German regulatory PUE. An observed constraint is often worth more than a costed promise. This analysis is of the “analysis” type: the firm’s reading, dated, open to discussion — it says so on it.
texte.Sous les onglets, deux listes : VOTRE RÔ: Under the tabs, two lists: YOUR ROLE then THE PATH. Seven reading paths — investor, bank, insurance, climatologist, water specialist, ESG analyst, and the investment envelope. Each one leads in the order that matters to the profession and names, at each step, THE TRAP specific to that profession. The second list offers only what makes sense for the chosen role, with the number of steps; a role with only one path starts without a second click. The “Guided path” button remains there to read the seven descriptions in full. The targeted section is highlighted, never hidden: you read the instruction and the data together.
texte.Sous les paramètres de programme, un dép: Below the programme parameters, a “DESIGN CRITERIA” drop-down opens seven settings, all optional. They come from the CONSEILPREV engineering framework — the data centre module of conseilprevcyber — which cites ASHRAE TC #, Directive (EU) #/# and its Delegated Regulation (EU) #/#, the Climate Neutral Data Centre Pact and ISO/IEC #. You can IMPOSE the cooling family instead of letting it be inferred from the country’s climate and water; choose the ALLOWABLE AIR CLASS, from A# to A#, which is the cheapest lever there is since it costs no equipment — but which engages the manufacturer’s warranty; impose a contractual PUE, which then takes precedence over any inference; set the LOAD RATE, bearing in mind that below # the partial-load penalty becomes the largest loss item, which the module then tells you in so many words; enter the PRICE of your electricity contract, which takes that item off the list of items that cannot be costed; enter the CARBON INTENSITY of your supply, using the GHG Protocol “market-based” approach, rather than the national average; and declare the contracted SHARE OF CARBON-FREE ENERGY, the REF indicator of EN #-#-#. Each value you enter switches the nature of the item concerned to ENTERED: the exported file will say that you are the one committing to it, not this framework. These criteria do NOT change the cost per megawatt — nothing in this framework would allow it. They change what happens afterwards: the PUE, hence the electricity, hence the total cost over ten years, that is, the only figure that separates two countries. Finally, two new blocks appear in the result: the EMBODIED CARBON of the construction, amortised per lot over its own lifetime — without it the comparison between a new build and a refurbishment is biased, and a CSRD file is incomplete from its first page — and the MARKET BENCHMARKS of the Climate Neutral Data Centre Pact, whose verdict is not “compliant” but “on target” or “to be justified”, because it is a voluntary commitment and not an obligation. An eighth criterion is deliberately missing: REDUNDANCY, which is nevertheless the largest cost multiplier of lots # and #. No source in this framework costs it; it therefore joins the list of items displayed empty, with the question to ask — a plausible but invented coefficient would be more dangerous than a blank box, because it would be believed.

An INVENTORY is displayed BEFORE any transfer — number of documents, size, themes, families, companies — then the transfer is done in batches with real progress. Each document keeps its ORIGINAL THEME word for word (“IEC #”, “EDF”…): that is the name you will look for it under. Sentinel pages are added on top, never instead.
